data.reasoning: The PKGBUILD and gamescope.install script are standard and safe, containing no malicious injections. The disagreement was solely due to Qwen experiencing API errors on .SRCINFO and .gitignore, which Deepseek successfully reviewed and cleared. Both models correctly identified the safe nature of the core packaging files.
data.disagreement_analysis: Qwen returned 'inconclusive' because it encountered HTTP 400 API errors when attempting to audit .SRCINFO and .gitignore. Deepseek successfully audited these files and found them safe. There was no actual security disagreement between the models on the files they both reviewed.
coverage_issues: Both models skipped 1908.patch, incorrectly classifying it as a binary file. Patch files are text-based and applied during the build process, so they must be reviewed for potential malicious code injections.
false_negatives: Potential missed malicious injection in 1908.patch, as it was skipped by both models due to incorrect binary classification.
learnings: The file classification logic incorrectly identified a .patch file as binary, causing it to be skipped. The tool should reliably identify text-based patch files and ensure they are reviewed, as they are applied during the build process and could contain injected code.

Transient API errors for non-critical metadata files (.SRCINFO, .gitignore) should not force an overall 'inconclusive' verdict if the core executable packaging files (PKGBUILD, .install) are successfully audited and found safe.
